name: Shiro RememberMe hardcoded / default cipher key (Shiro-550)
attack_scenario: Attacker takes the known/hardcoded key, encrypts a CommonsCollections (or similar) gadget with AES-CBC, sets it as the rememberMe cookie; Shiro decrypts and deserializes it, executing the gadget for remote code execution.
negative_test_hint: set the rememberMe cookie to a blob encrypted with the known default key "kPH+bIxk5D2deZiIxcaaaA==" and assert the server rejects it because the key comes from an environment secret

exemplar.explanation: Apache Shiro encrypts the RememberMe cookie with an AES key; older versions shipped the constant kPH+bIxk5D2deZiIxcaaaA== and countless tutorials copy it, so any attacker who knows the key can forge a cookie whose decrypted body is a Java deserialization gadget chain (Shiro-550, CVE-2016-4437). Loading the key from an environment secret means a cookie cannot be forged without also compromising the deployment environment.
